question: At the frozen policy's actual VLM call count, does CNN low-confidence selection outperform uniformly random selection?
design: Paired offline replay of archived full-test predictions; no training or new model inference
policy_selection: Reuse archived development-only max-probability policy. Reproduce development selection, do not retune on test.
primary_arms: Uniform random subset without replacement at exactly the archived route call count, 10000 replicates
Highest CNN confidence first at the same count, diagnostic negative control
secondary: Replay all ten archived development-selected probability/margin thresholds using batch-1 CNN scores. Keep every policy; do not select a new winner on test.
intervals: Random-subset 2.5/97.5 percentiles describe selection variation on this fixed test set. Paired image bootstrap describes route-minus-CNN and route-minus-full-VLM deltas with the existing policy fixed. Neither measures training seed or patient variability.
latency: No new latency measurements. Do not convert call count into claimed measured timing.
data_scope: Historical 3421-image BloodMNIST test with known duplicate limitations; not new blind or patient-independent testing. CNN is the original frozen WR50 feature extractor plus linear classifier, not the stronger fully fine-tuned CNN.
tie_break: Confidence-ranked negative control uses descending confidence, then ascending source_id; no labels used to choose mask.
source_archive_note: Original internal paths are provenance only; public replay inputs are per_image_replay.jsonl and results/fulltrain-20261005/.
